summary: A target-level plan of the effective residual comparison continuation: sharp newspace dimensions, removed-prime bounds, Kraus realization at the exact residual conductor, uniform two-torsion irreducibility and Lemos rational-isogeny uniformity. Every routed target in the first brief is planned; the other independent continuations have explicit split proposals. The plan is complete as a pass, not closed: recorded source and certificate gaps and supplier requests remain.

nodes.title: Kraus rationality threshold
nodes.statement: For positive N, μ(N)=[SL₂(ℤ):Γ₀(N)] and g⁺(N)=dimℂ S₂(Γ₀(N))new, define krausF(N)=(√(μ(N)/6)+1)^(2g⁺(N)), as a real number.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the supplier’s index and trivial-character newspace dimension; real division by 6 precedes the square root.
acceptance: At g⁺=0 the threshold is 1, not 0.

sources.match: Equation (7) defines the real square-root threshold with exponent twice the newspace dimension; the existing index and trivial-character newspace are used.
The displayed formulas agree with Kraus, including both square roots (checked on the PDF image; text extraction omits the radicals).

uses.how: Supplies the exact strict threshold for rationality and two-torsion preservation.
Computable cutoff at a prescribed residual conductor; users compare against a real number, keeping equality excluded.

nodes.title: Kraus two-torsion threshold
nodes.statement: For positive N define krausG(N)=(√(μ(lcm(4,N))/6)+1)^2, using the full level lcm(4,N), as a real number.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the same μ as krausF; lcm is taken before μ; the exponent is exactly 2.
acceptance: For N=1 and N=2 the value is 4.

hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.

acceptance: ℓ>krausH(N) is equivalent to both strict inequalities.

nodes.title: Martin’s sharp weight-two dimension bound
nodes.statement: For every positive N, 12g⁺(N)≤N+1. Equality holds exactly when N=35 or N is prime with N≡11 mod 12.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Import the general dimension formula and old/new decomposition from ModularForms 10C and Layer 3; obtain Martin’s multiplicative formula by Möbius convolution, rather than defining a second newspace.
Apply Martin Lemmas 16 and 19 for at most two prime factors. For at least three, use Lemmas 20–22 to reduce to 2^a3^b5^cp^d with 0≤a,b,c,d≤5 and 7≤p≤41.
Verify the 10,125 distinct remaining integers, and the finite checks below 1521 and 1548, by exact dimension formulas; derive the equality cases.
acceptance: N=1 gives 0; N=11 gives 1; N=35 gives 3; N=23 gives 2 and equality.

sources.locator: Theorem 2, p. 3; §4, Lemmas 16–22 and proof of Theorem 2, pp. 14–16 (v1)
sources.excerpt: There are 10,125 integers of this form
sources.match: Theorem 2 gives the bound and precisely the prime 11 mod 12 and N=35 equality cases; §4 proves it using Lemmas 16–22 and the finite calculation.

nodes.title: Effective congruence norm bound
nodes.statement: Let K be a number field of degree d, x∈𝒪K nonzero, λ a prime above the rational prime ℓ, and x∈λ. If |σ(x)|≤B for every embedding σ:K→ℂ and B≥0, then ℓ≤|NormK/ℚ(x)|≤B^d.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: The residue characteristic ℓ divides the ideal norm of λ, which divides Normℤ(x) by the baseline ideal-norm result.
Use norm nonvanishing and the all-embeddings product formula, with the integral/field norm comparison; bound each factor, including conjugate embeddings with their multiplicities.
acceptance: A bound at one distinguished embedding alone is insufficient; x=0 must be excluded.

sources.match: The norm step in Lemma 2.2 motivates this number-field adapter; the all-embeddings product and the separate integral/field-norm gap justify its stated generality.

nodes.title: Removed-prime exponent bound
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ have conductor M and minimal discriminant Δ, ℓ≥3 prime with E[ℓ] irreducible, and M₀ the reduced level of R20.6. If p≠ℓ is prime, p∥M and ℓ divides ordp(Δ), then ℓ≤(√p+1)^((M₀+1)/6).
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the supplier’s weight-two newform f at M₀ and the removed-prime congruence p+1≡±c_p modulo λ.
Every conjugate satisfies |σ(c_p)|≤2√p. Hence p+1∓c_p≠0 since p+1>2√p; bound the norm by (√p+1)^(2d).
The orbit degree d≤g⁺(M₀) and Martin’s bound give 2d≤(M₀+1)/6. Use the real power and base √p+1>1.
acceptance: The characteristic prime p=ℓ is excluded; additive primes are excluded; sign does not affect the bound.

sources.match: Lemma 2.2 retains p≠ℓ, p∥M and ℓ|ord_p(Δ); its proof combines the removed-prime congruence, all-embeddings norm and Martin bound.

nodes.title: Finite-prime rationality recognition
nodes.statement: For a normalized weight-two trivial-character newform f of level N, if c_q∈ℤ for every prime q≤μ(N)/6, then every coefficient c_n is in ℤ.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Galois conjugation preserves the normalized newform. Prime-power Hecke recurrences, including the bad-prime coefficients 0,±1, give equality of all coefficients n≤floor(μ(N)/6).
Apply characteristic-zero Sturm equality to f and each conjugate. Algebraic integrality then turns rational coefficients into integers.
acceptance: Only checking good primes is valid after separately proving integrality at primes dividing N.

sources.excerpt: Supposons que pour tout nombre premier
sources.match: Lemma 1 reconstructs the small composite coefficients from prime coefficients and then uses characteristic-zero Sturm equality and Galois conjugation.

nodes.title: Small-prime integrality above the Kraus threshold
nodes.statement: Let E/ℚ have irreducible E[ℓ], Serre weight 2, ℓ≥5 prime, and residual conductor N. For a weight-two trivial-character newform f realizing E[ℓ] at N, if ℓ>krausF(N), then c_q∈ℤ for all primes q≤μ(N)/6.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: If c_q is nonintegral, q∤N by the bad-prime formula. Since g⁺(N)≥1 and krausF(N)>μ(N)/6, q≠ℓ.
At good q use c_q≡a_q(E); at a removed multiplicative q use c_q≡±(q+1). The differences are nonzero because c_q is nonrational.
Hasse and purity bound every conjugate difference by (√q+1)^2; use the norm bound and degree≤g⁺(N) to obtain ℓ≤krausF(N), a contradiction.
acceptance: The case g⁺(N)=0 cannot admit the required newform.

sources.excerpt: Puisque al n’est pas dans Z
sources.match: Theorem 3 proof bounds the norm of a nonintegral coefficient difference, treating good and removed multiplicative primes separately; ℓ≥5, weight two and exact residual conductor remain explicit.

nodes.title: Rational newform comparison curve
nodes.statement: For a normalized weight-two trivial-character newform f of exact level N with all coefficients in ℤ, there exists an elliptic curve F/ℚ of exact conductor N with a_q(F)=c_q at good primes. If f realizes irreducible E[ℓ], then F[ℓ]≅E[ℓ] over ℚ.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Use the supplier’s J₀(N) newform quotient, of dimension one because the full coefficient field is ℚ; identify it as an elliptic curve with its origin.
Local-global compatibility proves exact conductor N, rather than merely a divisor; compare residual characteristic polynomials via Chebotarev and semisimplicity.
acceptance: The ℚℓ-dimension of the quotient Tate module is 2, not 2[N:ℚ]; reducible residuals require semisimplification.

sources.excerpt: cela signifie qu’il existe une courbe elliptique modulaire
sources.match: The rational-coefficient paragraph identifies a curve of exact conductor, then invokes residual irreducibility to obtain an isomorphism; the quotient and Galois comparisons are supplied separately.

nodes.title: Kraus’s rational comparison theorem
nodes.statement: For E/ℚ, prime ℓ≥5, irreducible E[ℓ] of Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ℓ conductor N, ℓ>krausF(N) implies there is F/ℚ of exact conductor N with F[ℓ]≅E[ℓ].
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Parent modularity supplies Kraus’s modularity assumption; take the exact-conductor residual newform.
Apply small-prime integrality, finite-prime rationality recognition and rational-newform realization.
acceptance: No full rational 2-torsion conclusion follows from this threshold alone.

sources.excerpt: les sous-groupes des points de p-torsion
sources.match: Theorem 3 requires modularity, irreducibility, weight two and ℓ≥5; unconditional parent modularity supplies its modularity hypothesis.

nodes.title: Finite recognition of point counts modulo four
nodes.statement: For E/ℚ of conductor N, 4 divides #E(𝔽q) at every prime q∤2N iff it does so for all such q≤μ(lcm(4,N))/6.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Import the ideal-valued Sturm congruence bound, not just analytic equality. Compare with the weight-two Γ₀(4) series Σ_{n odd}σ₁(n)q^n.
Deplete coefficients at primes dividing 2N using the source’s bad-prime conditions, transfer to lcm(4,N), and apply Kraus Appendix II Proposition 2 at the ideal 2ℤ squared.
Parent modularity identifies the elliptic L-series coefficients with the required newform.
acceptance: The full level lcm(4,N) and modulus 4 are required, rather than rad(N) and modulus 2.

sources.locator: Appendix II, Proposition 2 and Corollary, pp. 1158–1160
sources.match: The corollary is exactly finite recognition of good odd point counts modulo four at lcm(4,N); its bad-prime condition is automatic for elliptic multiplicative coefficients ±1.

nodes.title: Small-prime point-count transfer
nodes.statement: Let ℓ≥5 be prime, E/ℚ have full rational 2-torsion and irreducible E[ℓ] of Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ℓ conductor N. Let F/ℚ have exact conductor N and F[ℓ]≅E[ℓ] as Gℚ-representations. If ℓ>krausG(N), then for every prime q∤2N with q≤μ(lcm(4,N))/6, E has good reduction at q, a_q(E)=a_q(F), and 4 divides #F(𝔽q).
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: If E were bad at q while F is good, residual conductor comparison gives multiplicative reduction and a_q(F)≡±(q+1) mod ℓ; the nonzero integer difference is bounded by (√q+1)^2≤krausG(N).
At good q the two traces differ by a multiple of ℓ and have absolute difference≤4√q≤(√q+1)^2, so they are equal.
Good reduction at odd q injects rational 2-torsion; its four points imply the required divisibility.
acceptance: Strict ℓ>krausG(N) is necessary for these inequalities; q=ℓ cannot lie in the tested range.

sources.excerpt: Prouvons que E a bonne réduction en l.
sources.match: §3.3 proves good reduction at each tested odd prime and equality of the integral traces using the strict G threshold and Hasse bound.

nodes.title: Two-isogeny repair of rational two-torsion
nodes.statement: If E/ℚ satisfies 4|#E(𝔽q) for all but finitely many good odd q, then E is ℚ-isogenous by degree 1 or 2 to a curve F with full rational 2-torsion. For odd ℓ this isogeny preserves E[ℓ] and the conductor.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Chebotarev converts the congruence into constraints on each Galois element’s action on E[4]. Modulo 2 there is no order-3 image, so there is a fixed nonzero 2-torsion point P.
If the full 2-torsion is not rational, form E/⟨P⟩. The mod-4 constraints force both remaining 2-torsion directions of this quotient to be rational.
Use the dual isogeny to invert the degree-2 map on ℓ-torsion and the isogeny invariance of the ℓ-adic conductor.
acceptance: Do not conclude E itself has full rational 2-torsion from the point-count condition.

sources.excerpt: une isogénie définie sur Q de degré
sources.match: The final §3.3 paragraph invokes Serre IV-6 to produce an isogeny of degree one or two; the subgroup argument and finite-torsion Chebotarev step remain a recorded gap.

nodes.title: Kraus’s full-two-torsion realization
nodes.statement: If E/ℚ has full rational 2-torsion, ℓ≥5 is prime, E[ℓ] is irreducible of Serre weight 2 and prime-to-ℓ conductor N, and ℓ>krausH(N), then some F/ℚ has exact conductor N, full rational 2-torsion, and F[ℓ]≅E[ℓ].
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Use krausH’s two inequalities. Obtain F₀ from Kraus’s rational comparison theorem.
Transfer the tested point counts, propagate them by finite mod-four recognition, and apply two-isogeny repair to F₀.
The repair preserves the odd residual representation and exact conductor.
acceptance: Both hypotheses “Serre weight 2” and “exact prime-to-ℓ conductor N” remain explicit.

sources.excerpt: ayant tous ses points d’ordre 2 rationnels sur Q
sources.match: Theorem 4 combines the F and G bounds, retains irreducibility and Serre weight two, and repairs full rational two-torsion through a two-isogeny.

nodes.title: Reduced-level adapter for Kraus’s theorem
nodes.statement: In an application with reduced level M₀ from R20.6, Kraus’s full-two-torsion theorem applies at M₀ only after establishing Serre weight 2 and N(E[ℓ])=M₀. In particular, for ℓ≥5 and ℓ∤M, local conductor comparison gives N(E[ℓ])=M₀; weight 2 must still be checked (for example by finite flatness at ℓ).
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: At each q≠ℓ, additive exponents agree and multiplicative exponent 1 drops exactly when ℓ|ordq(Δ). At ℓ∤M there is no coefficient-prime factor left in M₀.
Use the supplier’s finite-flat weight recipe where it applies; substitute the proved equality into Kraus’s theorem, without identifying the carriers by definition.
acceptance: If ℓ divides M and remains in M₀, then M₀ cannot be the prime-to-ℓ conductor.

sources.match: This is an application adapter, not a verbatim Bennett–Siksek theorem: equality with the quotient level needs the local conductor theorem and ℓ∤M; the weight-two hypothesis remains separate.

nodes.title: Mazur’s prime-isogeny theorem
nodes.statement: If E/ℚ admits a cyclic rational isogeny of prime degree r, then r∈{2,3,5,7,11,13,17,19,37,43,67,163}. For non-CM E the possibilities are {2,3,5,7,11,13,17,37}.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Identify the isogeny with a noncuspidal rational point on X₀(r). Follow Mazur’s four-step route: cuspidal formal immersion into the Eisenstein quotient; finiteness of its rational points; potentially good reduction and the isogeny character; Frobenius congruences.
The character exponents 0,1/3,1/2 reduce the possibilities by the p=3 and p=5 calculations and the imaginary quadratic class-number-one theorem.
Use the complete rational-point lists in Theorem 7.1 to discard the CM-only degrees 19,43,67,163 for non-CM curves. This uses geometric CM, not Endℚ(E).
acceptance: A CM curve can have a rational 163-isogeny; it is excluded only from the non-CM list.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, pp. 129–130; proof outline pp. 132–133; Theorem 7.1, pp. 153–155
sources.excerpt: The object of this paper is to show
sources.match: Theorem 1 gives the prime list; Theorem 7.1 identifies the CM-only degrees. The arithmetic proof inputs remain explicit gaps rather than consequences of moduli geometry.

nodes.title: Two-torsion isogeny exclusions
nodes.statement: For every prime ℓ≥11, no elliptic curve over ℚ admits a cyclic rational 2ℓ-isogeny. For every prime ℓ≥7, none admits a cyclic rational 4ℓ-isogeny.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Use Mazur’s prime list to reduce the odd prime degrees to a finite set.
For ℓ≥11 the forbidden composite degrees 2ℓ follow from the rational cyclic-degree classification; the 4ℓ exclusions for ℓ≥7 follow from the same classification.
The required classification is the Mazur–Kenku list n≤19 or n∈{21,25,27,37,43,67,163}. The unresolved source verification is a recorded gap, not attributed to Mazur’s prime theorem.
acceptance: 2·7=14 is allowed; neither threshold can be extended just by dropping its inequality.

sources.match: Bennett–Siksek state the irreducibility consequences. The stronger intermediate composite-degree exclusions require the separately recorded Mazur–Kenku classification input; they are not quoted as a theorem of this passage.

nodes.title: Two-torsion kernel transport
nodes.statement: For odd prime ℓ, if E/ℚ has a rational cyclic ℓ-subgroup and a rational point of order 2, it admits a rational cyclic 2ℓ-isogeny. If all E[2] is rational, some curve isogenous to E admits a rational cyclic 4ℓ-isogeny.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: For one 2-point, take the sum of the coprime stable kernels; it is cyclic of order 2ℓ.

For full 2-torsion, choose distinct nonzero P,Q∈E[2](ℚ). On E′=E/⟨P⟩ compose the dual map E′→E with E→E/⟨Q⟩; its kernel is stable cyclic of order 4, since the preimages of Q double to the nonzero dual kernel point.
Transport the ℓ-kernel through the 2-isogeny, then sum it with the cyclic 4-kernel.
acceptance: A full rational E[2] is itself noncyclic; directly adding it to an ℓ-kernel does not produce a cyclic 4ℓ-kernel.

sources.locator: Mazur input in Lemmas 3.3 and 3.5, pp. 362–363
sources.excerpt: we know from the work of Mazur
sources.match: This is the kernel argument explaining the two-torsion irreducibility applications, not a verbatim source lemma: coprime cyclic kernels give 2ℓ; distinct rational two-points and dual isogeny give cyclic 4ℓ on an isogenous curve.

nodes.title: Irreducibility with full rational two-torsion
nodes.statement: If E/ℚ has full rational 2-torsion and ℓ≥7 is prime, E[ℓ] is irreducible over 𝔽ℓ; since it is odd, it is absolutely irreducible.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: A proper nonzero invariant subspace is a line, hence a stable cyclic ℓ-subgroup.
Kernel transport gives a rational cyclic 4ℓ-isogeny on an isogenous curve; apply the exclusion theorem.
Use oddness and the distinct ±1 eigenvalues of complex conjugation to upgrade irreducibility for odd ℓ.
acceptance: No non-CM hypothesis is used.

sources.match: Lemma 3.3 uses the full-two-torsion irreducibility threshold ℓ≥7. This node isolates that reusable conclusion; oddness supplies absolute irreducibility.

nodes.title: Irreducibility with a rational two-torsion point
nodes.statement: If E/ℚ has a rational point of order 2 and ℓ≥11 is prime, E[ℓ] is irreducible over 𝔽ℓ and absolutely irreducible.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: An invariant line gives a cyclic ℓ-subgroup. Combine it with the rational 2-point and exclude the resulting cyclic 2ℓ-isogeny.
Upgrade by oddness as for the full-two-torsion case.
acceptance: A curve with a 14-isogeny supplies a boundary counterexample at ℓ=7.

sources.match: Lemma 3.5 uses the one-two-point threshold ℓ≥11. This node isolates that reusable conclusion; oddness supplies absolute irreducibility.

nodes.title: Potential good reduction in the nonsplit Cartan case
nodes.statement: If p≥5 is prime and ρ̄E,p(Gℚ) is contained in the normalizer of a nonsplit Cartan, then E has potentially good reduction at each rational prime q with q≢±1 mod p, and also at q=p.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: If potentially multiplicative, write the local representation as a quadratic twist of a Tate-curve representation with eigencharacters ψχp,ψ.
Squaring sends each image element into the nonsplit Cartan; a split pair of eigenvalues there must coincide, forcing χp²=1.
At q=p the cyclotomic character is surjective, contradicting p≥5. At q≠p its unramified Frobenius value q forces q²≡1 mod p.
acceptance: At q=p the congruence exception cannot excuse potentially multiplicative reduction.

sources.excerpt: If ℓ = p, then we know that χp surjects
sources.match: Proposition 2.2 proves the criterion by squaring Tate eigencharacters; its proof includes q=p via surjectivity of the local cyclotomic character.

nodes.title: Chen’s isogeny at rational-isogeny level
nodes.statement: For r∈{1,2,3,5,7,13} and prime p∉{1,2,3,5,7,13}, the Jacobian of X₀(r)×X(1)Xns⁺(p) is ℚ-isogenous to the p-new quotient of Jac(X₀⁺(rp²)), by a correspondence commuting with T_n for gcd(n,p)=1. Here X₀⁺(rp²) denotes the smooth projective normalization of X₀(r)×X(1)(X₀(p²)/⟨w_{p²}⟩), equivalently X₀(rp²)/⟨w_{p²}⟩; it is not the quotient by w_{rp²}. The mixed nonsplit curve is the smooth compactification of its level-moduli fiber product.
hypotheses: All quantifiers and hypotheses are included explicitly in the statement.
proofSteps: Construct X′(p)=X(p)/(Nsp∩Nns) and the split/nonsplit projection correspondence.
Under Xsp⁺(p)≅X₀⁺(p²), the p-old divisors map to old divisors; the target’s r-level old Jacobian vanishes since X₀(r) has genus zero.
Apply Chen’s explicit-isogeny identification, retaining the away-from-p Hecke equivariance.
acceptance: p-old means degeneracy from level rp, not the full oldspace at level rp².
The Atkin–Lehner involution acts on the p²-level only and retains the r-level structure.

nodes.title: Rank-zero winding quotient

nodes.title: Cuspidal formal immersion at isogeny level
nodes.statement: Let Σ={2,3,5,7,13}, r∈Σ, p∉Σ be prime, K=ℚ(ζp)⁺ and R=ℤ[1/p,ζp]⁺. Let X be the canonical mixed nonsplit modular curve X₀,ns⁺(r,p) over R, c an R-valued cusp, J its generic-fiber Jacobian, and π:J→A a nonzero optimal ℚ-quotient with A(ℚ) finite and kernel stable under T_n for gcd(n,p)=1. Let 𝒜 be the Néron model of A and φ:Xˢᵐ→𝒜 the extension of π∘[P↦(P)−(c)]. At a prime 𝔮|q of R, with q≠p prime and q≡±1 mod p, φ is a formal immersion at c_𝔮. For a noncuspidal P∈X(ℚ), φ(P) is torsion in A(K). These are the Lemos extension targets; the required canonical model and the extension of the proof beyond r=2,3 remain gaps.

Since p outside Σ is at least 11, q≡±1 mod p implies q>3 and q∤r. There is no residue-characteristic-2 case here. Use unramified torsion specialization at the denominator prime, with good reduction of A at q verified from the exact model.
For rational P, Galois differences of (P)−(c) are cuspidal divisors. Manin–Drinfeld makes them torsion, so a multiple of φ(P) is in finite A(ℚ): this is Lemma 8.3.

proofSteps: Import the verified modular-curve models and j-map identity, rather than treat a rational function as a modular curve by definition.
Write t=a/b in lowest terms with b>0. Since f_r is monic, integrality forces b|a^(r+1), whence b=1; then integrality forces a|f_r(0).
Enumerate both signs of every nonzero divisor of the constant term and deduplicate j-values.
